messages.author: 9bab4c98a6acda91
messages.subject: filtering out linked loci
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to estimate effective population size from a SNP dataset that I have, and I'd like to exclude linked loci before I do this. I have two questions regarding doing this using the dartR package.

1. I've used gl.report.ld to get a file showing r2 values, which I'd like to use for filtering, but the loci labels in the output don't correspond to the names of my loci, so I'm not sure how to identify these loci based on the output.

2. Is there the option of directly filtering out loci e.g. using something like gl.filter.ld based on r2 values?   

Thanks!

Shandiya

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: filtering out linked loci
parts:
Hi Shandiya,

First port of call would be to remove secondary SNPs from your dataset, that is, multiple SNPs scored from the one sequence tag. They are obviously linked.

The relevant functions are gl.report.secondaries(gl) and gl.filter.secondaries(gl).

As for the substance of your question, the person who wrote the ld scripts (Bernd) is on leave, and may not be able to respond for a couple of weeks.

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Re: filtering out linked loci
parts:
Hi James,

 

Half the answer is:

 

The loci names are not returned but their number in the order of your genlight object, so for example you can do:

 

> ldf <- gl.report.ld(possums.gl)

Start to calculate LD for all pairs of loci...

Using 1 cores in 2  chunks.

Depending on the number of loci this may take a while...

nchunks specifies the number of steps in the progress bar and the number of intermediate saves, but slows the computation a bit. nchunks = 1 is fastest.

Seperate all 300 loci...

Generate all possible pairs: 19900 ...

Calculate LD for all pairs...

 

# Simulations: 19900 . Took 13 seconds.

 

Results are saved as object LDallp under LDallp.rdata.

Once you have checked you can delete your LD_chunks_  files.

> ldf$loc1name <- locNames(possums.gl)[ldf$loc1]

> ldf$loc2name <- locNames(possums.gl)[ldf$loc2]

 

 

The last two lines add the names of the loci to the output data frame.

 

 

In terms of filtering we do not have a function yet, but happy to write one. It is a bit “tricky” and will not happen in the next 2 weeks.

 

The reason why a bit more involved is because the r2 value (if used as a threshold) is for pairs of loci and you basically have to decide which of the two you want to “kick” out (obviously you can also simply kick out both) but if you want to keep most loci then a stepwise approach is smarter.

 

As an example think about you have 3 loci, so three pairwise comparison  1-2, 1-3 and 2-3. Assuming 1-2 and 2-3 are in ld and you want to kick them out, then by kicking out loci of both pairs all loci are gone. If you instead kick out loci 2 and 1-3 are not linked then you would have two loci left to work with. So such a filter is more efficient than just simply using the threshold for all pairs at once.

 

 

In case you are versatile in R and want to write it yourself please send me the script.

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

In case you are fine to kick out all loci pairs you can use

 

> index <- ldf$R2>0.1
> table(index)

 

index
FALSE  TRUE 
19178   722

 

So 722 pairs are higher than 0.1 (my chosen threshold, this is a simulated data set so I would not expect any high R2)

 

barplot(table(c(ldf$loc1name[index], ldf$loc2name[index])), las=2)

 

 

So a smart approach would be now to get rid of loci 160 (is 32 times linked with another loci) and then check again the pairs remove the one with most lds and so on).

 

 

 

Back to the simple filter, you need now to create the index and filter:

 

 

> locisout <- unique(c(ldf$loc1name[index], ldf$loc2name[index]))
> locisout
  [1] "X1"   "X2"   "X3"   "X4"   "X5"   "X6"   "X7"   "X8"   "X11" 
 [10] "X12"  "X14"  "X15"  "X16"  "X17"  "X18"  "X19"  "X20"  "X21" 
 [19] "X22"  "X24"  "X25"  "X26"  "X27"  "X29"  "X30"  "X31"  "X32"

This creates the names of locis above the threshold (in any pair) and finally to filter your genlight object

 

 

!(locNames(possums.gl) %in% locisout)   #an index which loci should be not used (out=TRUE)

 

poss.filld <- possums.gl[, !(locNames(possums.gl) %in% locisout)]

 

 

This filters the loci (and leaves the one in which are below the threshold all the time over all pairs)

 

Do not forget to update also the meta data via:

 

poss.filld@other$loc.metrics <- poss.filld@other$loc.metrics[!(locNames(possums.gl) %in% locisout),]

 

 

[possums.gl does not have one, but your data set has most often metadata ]

 

Hope that helps,

 

Bernd
